questions.solutionHtml:
Proteins
  • The thermic effect of food (TEF) refers to the increase in energy expenditure that occurs during the digestion, absorption, and metabolism of nutrients in the body. This effect varies depending on the macronutrient composition of the food consumed. Let's examine each option in detail and discuss their thermic effects:
  • Proteins: Proteins have the highest thermic effect among the three macronutrients. When you consume protein-rich foods, your body needs to expend more energy to break down and process the proteins. This is because proteins are composed of amino acids, and the body requires energy to convert them into usable forms. The thermic effect of proteins ranges from 20% to 30% of the total caloric intake from protein.

questions.stem: What is the order of drawing blood sample in vials/vacutainers:
questions.solutionHtml:
Blue, Red, Lavender, Grey
  • The correct order of drawing blood samples in vials/vacutainers is Blue, Red, Lavender, Grey.
  • Different vials or vacutainers are used to collect specific types of blood samples for various laboratory tests. Each color-coded tube is designed to preserve and stabilize specific components of the blood. The correct order mentioned above follows this sequence:
  • Blue: The blue-top tube is typically used for coagulation tests that require blood to be collected in citrate anticoagulant. The citrate in the tube helps prevent blood clotting by binding calcium.

questions.stem: Which amino acid is not used for synthesis of hormones?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glycine
  • Glycine is an amino acid that does not directly participate in the synthesis of hormones. While glycine is an important amino acid involved in many biological processes, including the synthesis of proteins, it is not a precursor for hormone synthesis.
  • On the other hand, tyrosine, phenylalanine, and tryptophan are all aromatic amino acids that serve as building blocks for the synthesis of various hormones.

questions.stem: Liver produces KB but cannot use KB due to absence of which enzyme:
questions.solutionHtml:
Thiophorase
  • Thiophorase, also known as succinyl-CoA:3-ketoacid CoA transferase, is the enzyme that is absent in the liver, preventing it from using ketone bodies (KB) as a fuel source.
  • The liver plays a crucial role in ketone body metabolism. During periods of prolonged fasting or low carbohydrate intake, the liver produces ketone bodies (acetoacetate and β-hydroxybutyrate) through a process called ketogenesis. These ketone bodies are then released into the bloodstream and can be used as an alternative fuel source by various tissues, including the brain, heart, and skeletal muscles.
  • However, the liver lacks the enzyme thiophorase (succinyl-CoA:3-ketoacid CoA transferase) necessary to utilize the ketone bodies it produces. This enzyme is required to convert acetoacetate into acetoacetyl-CoA, which can then be further metabolized into two molecules of acetyl-CoA. Acetyl-CoA is a central molecule in energy metabolism and can enter the citric acid cycle (also known as the Kreb’s cycle) to produce ATP.
  • Due to the absence of thiophorase in the liver, the liver cannot use ketone bodies as an energy source. Instead, the liver releases ketone bodies into the bloodstream for other tissues to utilize. This allows other organs, particularly the brain, to switch to ketone bodies as a fuel source during periods of fasting or carbohydrate restriction, preserving glucose for organs that depend on it, such as red blood cells and certain parts of the brain.

questions.stem: In Pompe’s disease, enzyme deficiency is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lysosomal acid alpha glucosidase
  • Pompe's disease, also known as glycogen storage disease type II or acid maltase deficiency, is a rare genetic disorder characterized by the deficiency or absence of the enzyme lysosomal acid alpha glucosidase (also called acid alpha-glucosidase or acid maltase). This enzyme is responsible for breaking down glycogen, a complex sugar molecule, into glucose within the lysosomes of cells.
  • In individuals with Pompe's disease, the deficiency of lysosomal acid alpha glucosidase leads to the accumulation of glycogen in various tissues, particularly the muscles. This glycogen buildup affects the proper functioning of cells and tissues, causing a wide range of symptoms, primarily affecting the muscles and respiratory system.

questions.stem: A patient with C/O muscle weakness came to OPD. Doctor found he has cardiomyopathy & diagnosed him to be a case of Barth syndrome, where patient has mitochondrial dysfunction. What is the defect in this patient:
questions.solutionHtml:
Cardiolipin
  • The defect in this patient is Barth syndrome, which is characterized by muscle weakness and cardiomyopathy, is related to Cardiolipin.
  • Barth syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects males and is caused by mutations in gene responsible for the production of an enzyme involved in cardiolipin synthesis.
  • Cardiolipin is a unique phospholipid primarily found in the inner mitochondrial membrane, where it plays a crucial role in maintaining mitochondrial structure and function.
  • The defective cardiolipin affects several mitochondrial processes, including energy production, electron transport chain function, and mitochondrial membrane stability.
  • The mitochondrial dysfunction observed in Barth syndrome contributes to the symptoms of muscle weakness and cardiomyopathy seen in affected individuals.

questions.stem: A 15-year old boy, a known case of type I DM, undergoes the following test for the detection of KB. Which is this test:
questions.solutionHtml:
Rothera’s Test
  • The test used for the detection of ketone bodies (KB) in the given scenario of a 15-year-old boy with type I diabetes mellitus is Rothera's Test.
  • Rothera's Test is a commonly used laboratory test to detect the presence of ketone bodies, specifically acetoacetate, in urine or blood samples. It is particularly relevant in the context of diabetes mellitus, as individuals with uncontrolled diabetes, especially type I diabetes, may experience an increase in ketone production.
  • In type I diabetes, the body is unable to produce sufficient insulin, resulting in a lack of glucose utilization by cells for energy. As a result, the body begins to break down fats as an alternative energy source, leading to the production of ketone bodies, including acetoacetate.
  • Rothera's Test involves the reaction of acetoacetate with sodium nitroprusside and glycine in an alkaline medium. This reaction forms a purple-colored complex, indicating the presence of ketone bodies.
  • On the other hand, the other options listed are not specific tests for the detection of ketone bodies in this context:

Vitamin B6 deficiency
  • Xanthurenic assay a.k.a. Tryptophan load test. Xanthurenic acid in urine indicates Vitamin B6 deficiency.
  • Xanthurenic acid is a metabolite that is formed during the breakdown of the amino acid tryptophan. Under normal conditions, tryptophan is metabolized along the kynurenine pathway, which involves the conversion of tryptophan to various intermediate compounds. One of these intermediates is xanthurenic acid.
  • In individuals with a deficiency of vitamin B6 (pyridoxine), the conversion of tryptophan to niacin (vitamin B3) is impaired. As a result, tryptophan is metabolized through an alternative pathway, leading to the accumulation of xanthurenic acid. Therefore, the presence of xanthurenic acid in urine is indicative of a vitamin B6 deficiency.
  • It's worth noting that the other options listed, including b) Vitamin B1 deficiency, c) Niacin deficiency, and d) Vitamin B2 deficiency, are not directly associated with the presence of xanthurenic acid in urine. questions.stem: Which of the following is false about collagen:

options.label: B
options.text: Collagan is a type of fibrous protein, which is most abundant of all human proteins

options.label: C
options.text: Post translational hydroxylation of proline & lysine

options.label: D
options.text: Triple helix is required for its function

questions.solutionHtml:
Most abundant AA is Phenyl-alanine
  • The false statement about collagen is: Most abundant AA is Phenyl-alanine.
  • Collagen is a fibrous protein that is indeed the most abundant protein in the human body. It provides structural support to various tissues, including skin, bones, tendons, and blood vessels. However, the most abundant amino acid in collagen is actually glycine, not phenylalanine. Glycine makes up approximately one-third of the amino acids in the collagen protein chain.

questions.stem: The base sequence of the strand of DNA used as the template for transcription has the base sequence GATCTAC. What is the base sequence of RNA product?
questions.solutionHtml:
GUAGAUC
  • The base sequence of RNA formed is exactly same as non-template strand which in this case is 5’ GTAGATC 3’.
  • We have to just replace the T with U to get the RNA sequence. So RNA sequence is: 5’ GUAGAUC 3’
